newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall, further declines seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall, further declines seen.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index eased 1.15 percent on Monday on lack of demand from foreign and domestic investors and traders said the index could lose up to five percent this week.

"International demand is low partly due to the holiday season and partly due to the fact that foreign investors are waiting for prices to ease a bit in order to buy shares cheaper later," one broker said.
"I think shares could fall by up to another five percent this week as foreigners are not buying which consequently diminishes domestic investor's interest," she added.
An upswing could only be expected in the second half of August when buyers are expected to start coming back for a fresh investment cycle in September, another trader said.
The SBI index fell 17.82 points to 1,534.84.
Pharmaceutical producer Lek was most actively traded, down 0.7 percent to 35,250 tolars on volume of 2,348 shares for total turnover of 82.6 million tolars.
Ordinary shares of trader Kovinotehna led decliners, down 5.43 percent to 522 tolars on volume of 4,368 shares. Traders attributed the fall to poor liquidity of the stock.
Construction company GPG was the top gainer, up 1.64 percent to 6,200 on volume of 45 shares.

Traders said drug makers Lek and Krka and trader Mercator are considered to be the best investment in the short-term as these shares remain among the most liquid on the market and foreign interest in them is seen as strong.
